text: Everything from Lessons Forty-Eight through Fifty genuinely fits together into one real pipeline, moving a data factory from a developer's feature branch all the way to production.

Git handles dev-side collaboration — feature branches merge via pull request into the collaboration branch. Publishing pushes that into ADF Dev and writes ARM templates to the publish branch. Release Management pulls that publish branch as an artifact and deploys it, as an ARM environment, to ADF Test, then separately to ADF Prod.

A genuinely important, easy-to-miss rule: only the development factory should ever be connected to Git. Test and production factories are updated exclusively through the release pipeline or a manually deployed ARM template — never authored directly, never Git-connected themselves. Wanting to edit a pipeline directly in production is a sign something about the process has gone wrong.

If dev, test, and production all deploy from the exact same ARM template, how does each end up pointing at its own storage account, its own SQL server? Global parameters — factory-wide values referenced throughout your pipelines, overridden per environment at deployment time. The same mechanism, combined with an If Condition activity, unlocks real feature flags: logic that runs in dev but stays dormant in production, with no duplicated pipeline required.

Data Factory genuinely doesn't support publishing a subset of your changes. Publishing means everything currently in the collaboration branch, every single time — because entities depend on each other, and partial publishing risks leaving the factory in a real, inconsistent state. Need a narrow, urgent fix without dragging along unrelated work? That's what a dedicated hotfix process is for, not selective publishing.

One full lifecycle diagram, a hard rule about which environments touch Git, and the global-parameter mechanism that makes one template serve three real environments. Next: ARM Templates and Azure DevOps Pipelines — actually building the release pipeline behind everything in this diagram.
